cases.answer: 3M's FY2022 GAAP operating margin decreased to 19.1% from 20.8% in FY2021, a decline of 1.7 percentage points. The key drivers were: (1) net costs for significant litigation (Combat Arms Earplugs and PFAS-related) had a large negative impact; (2) PFAS manufacturing exit costs; (3) raw material and logistics cost inflation; and (4) Russia exit charges and divestiture costs. These were partially offset by the gain on the Food Safety divestiture and organic sales growth/productivity improvements. Excluding special items, adjusted operating margin was 20.8% in FY2022 versus 22.2% in FY2021, reflecting mainly raw material inflation and operational headwinds. Operating margin remains useful, but 3M supplements it with adjusted measures because special items can significantly distort year-over-year comparisons.

cases.answer: No. Operating margin is not a meaningful metric for American Express because it is a payments/financial services company that reports total revenues net of interest expense and includes provisions for credit losses as a core expense; a standard operating margin based on operating expenses alone would omit these significant items. Better indicators are pretax margin or return on average equity. On a pretax basis, margin was 11.9% in 2020, 25.2% in 2021, and 18.1% in 2022, so the 2022 profile declined from 2021 rather than improved; return on average equity also declined from 33.7% in 2021 to 32.3% in 2022.

cases.answer: Gross margin is not a useful or disclosed metric for American Express. As a globally integrated payments and financial services company, American Express does not report gross margin or cost of goods sold. Its results are driven by total revenues net of interest expense, provisions for credit losses, and operating expenses such as Card Member rewards, business development, Card Member services, marketing, salaries, and other expenses. For FY2022, total revenues net of interest expense increased 25% to $52.9 billion, primarily due to higher discount revenue from increased billed business, higher net card fees, and higher net interest income. However, pretax income decreased 10% to $9.6 billion, largely because provisions for credit losses increased to $2.2 billion (versus a net release in 2021) and expenses rose 24%, driven by higher rewards and services costs, business development, and net losses on Amex Ventures investments. Therefore, changes in profitability are better analyzed through net interest margin, expense ratios, and credit loss provisions rather than gross margin.
cases.publisher_answer: Performance is not measured through gross margin
cases.assessment: Correctly rejects gross margin as disclosed measure. Supplemental revenue/provision/expense details need source checking.
